note: V90BitsToSymbol's three arithmetic members, against t_v90btsproc.  The placement mutations move a loop bound, a store or a status; the DIAGNOSTIC ones swap the two error messages, which writes the same bytes into the object and is only catchable through the transcript.  NOT here: turning `wanted * bitsPerFrame / 6` into `(wanted / 6) * bitsPerFrame` on the exact arm.  The two agree for every value that arm can be given -- the arm is chosen by `wanted % 6 == 0` -- so it is equivalent by construction, and what holds the object's spelling there is finding 617's full-text identity, not a test.

why: EXPECTED UNCAUGHT, and it is a property of the arithmetic rather than a gap in the sweep.  On the underflow arm `symbolsDone < symbolsBlockSize`, so the leftover shift `for (i = symbolsBlockSize; i < symbolsDone; i++)` cannot run whether the zero was stored or not, `kept` stays 0, and `symbolsDone = kept` writes the same zero four lines later.  The store is in the reconstruction because the blob has `movl $0x0,0x10(%ebp)` at 0x2fded and then `mov %ebx,0x10(%ebp)` at 0x2fe1e -- two stores to +0x10 on one path -- and because it is what lets the compiler constant-propagate the loop bound to the `xor %esi,%esi` at 0x2fdf4.  So this one line rests on the instructions and not on the suite.
